# Development screen on UCI 257

The published User Knowledge Modeling workbook contains separate training and test sheets. Read only Training_Data. Use the five released study and exam covariates to predict the recorded knowledge category after the two exam scores are available. UCI reports algorithm-assisted classification of knowledge states. The labels support a table-classification endpoint. Treating them as independently measured mastery would require other evidence.

Freeze a five-fold shuffled stratified outer development split (seed 257). For each outer fold use four-fold stratified cross-fitting in its complement to produce out-of-fit confidence and correctness observations. Standardize the five predictors on the respective fitting split and use L2 multinomial logistic regression with C=1 for every issued label. Temperature scaling fits a scalar by minimizing inner log loss in log-temperature bounds [-3,3]. Learn a logistic correctness detector on inner max probability, top-two probability margin, normalized entropy, one-hot predicted class and standardized five covariates (C=1). For each new row estimate local correctness by the fraction of correctly classified inner observations among its 15 nearest neighbors in the standardized original features, with two pseudo-observations centered on the global inner accuracy. A fixed equal combination of detector and local correctness is the candidate. Include both components, maximum probability, calibrated maximum probability, margin and k-neighbor predicted-class agreement (15 neighbors) as controls. All methods rank the identical fixed predictions. At equal confidence break ties by source row number. Score AURC as the mean of cumulative error fractions over every nonempty accepted prefix; average the five fold AURCs equally. Report original mean differences and foldwise signs. Require an improvement of at least .02 AURC versus every control in development before using the reserved test. This screen measures performance on one development set, so a passing screen would still require stronger published baselines and confirmatory evaluation.
